questions.text: In the past few weeks, have you wished you were dead?
In the past few weeks, have you felt that you or your family would be better off if you were dead?
In the past week, have you been having thoughts about killing yourself?
Have you ever tried to kill yourself?
If yes, when was the most recent attempt?
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself right now?

title: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ)
about: NIMH's suicide risk screen for patients aged 8 and over in medical settings: four yes or no questions asked by a nurse or clinician, and an acuity question when any is answered Yes. It has no total: the result is a negative, non-acute positive or acute positive screen.

licence.terms: A public domain tool, free of charge (NIMH ASQ Toolkit).

source.name: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) Suicide Risk Screening Tool, NIMH Toolkit (revised 9/29/25)

rules_source.citation: NIMH Toolkit, Suicide Risk Screening Tool for youth and adults (revised 9/29/25); Horowitz LM, Bridge JA, Teach SJ, et al. Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med. 2012;166(12):1170-1176; Horowitz LM, Snyder DJ, Boudreaux ED, et al. Psychosomatics. 2020;61(6):713-722.
rules_source.stated: Tool: "If patient answers Yes to any of Questions #1 through #4, ask the following acuity question: 5." Next steps: "No to all Questions #1-#4: Negative screen"; "Yes to any of Questions #1-#4 and... Yes to Question #5: Acute positive screen (imminent/acute risk identified)"; "...No to Question #5: Non-acute positive screen (potential risk identified)". Information sheet: "Positive screen: 'yes' to any of the 4 items"; "Public domain tool, free of charge". Adult validation (medical inpatients): PMID 32487323.
